title: Do LLM-judges Align with Human Relevance in Cranfield-style Recommender Evaluation?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing offline evaluation metrics based on historical logged interactions against LLM-judge scores by testing candidate recommender models, specifically observing how the LLM-judge favors a model variant equipped with a popularity debiasing mechanism that traditional offline metrics penalize.

Measuring the completeness of relevance labels (using the Judged@100 metric) and recommender system ranking agreement across traditional historical train-test splits, Cranfield-style pooling, and LLM-judges to demonstrate how LLMs mitigate biases toward items previously exposed by production systems or selected during pooling.
